title: Lagaan Returns to Theatres for Three Days Only. Twenty-Five Years Later, It Still Makes You Want to Stand Up and Cheer.
excerpt: The Oscar-nominated cricket epic that turned a dusty village into the most famous pitch in Indian cinema is back on the big screen — June 12 to 14. Here's why you shouldn't miss it.
body:
There is a shot in **Lagaan** where **Bhuvan** looks up at the sky, waiting for rain, and an entire village holds its breath with him. Twenty-five years after that shot first flickered across Indian screens, it still works. The dust is still golden. The silence is still unbearable. And when the rain finally comes, you still feel it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=hTt5FbgziPw</youtube>

**Aamir Khan Productions** announced this week that *Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India* will return to cinemas for a special three-day theatrical run on **June 12, 13, and 14** — marking the film's 25th anniversary with the kind of event it deserves. A newly cut re-release trailer dropped alongside the announcement, and within hours, the nostalgia hit harder than a Bhuvan sixer.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZHaOT0gGnv/

## The Film That Changed Everything

Directed by **Ashutosh Gowariker** and produced by and starring Aamir Khan, *Lagaan* did something no Indian film had done in decades — it made the world pay attention. Set in 1893 during the British Raj, the story follows the villagers of Champaner as they challenge their colonial rulers to a high-stakes cricket match. Win, and the crushing *lagaan* (tax) is waived for three years. Lose, and they pay triple.

The premise sounds like a fable. The execution was cinema at its most ambitious. With an ensemble cast featuring **Gracy Singh**, **Rachel Shelley**, **Paul Blackthorne**, **Raghubir Yadav**, and **Rajesh Vivek**, and costumes by the legendary Oscar-winning designer **Bhanu Athaiya**, every frame of the film was crafted with the kind of obsessive detail that Aamir Khan became famous for.

And then there was the music.

## A.R. Rahman's Masterclass

**A.R. Rahman's** soundtrack for *Lagaan* remains one of the most complete albums in Hindi cinema. *Ghanan Ghanan* still evokes monsoon clouds gathering over cracked earth. *Mitwa* still brings the lump to your throat. *Radha Kaise Na Jale* still belongs in every wedding playlist in the diaspora. *O Rey Chhori* still makes you want to dance in the aisles.

The background score during the cricket match — all forty-five minutes of it — is a masterclass in tension-building that Hans Zimmer would tip his hat to. Hearing it in a theatre, with proper surround sound, is a different experience entirely from watching it on your laptop at 2 AM.

> "A timeless epic that touched every heart. On the 25th Anniversary of LAGAAN, the epic saga returns to the big screen." — Aamir Khan Productions

## The Oscar That Almost Was

*Lagaan* was nominated for the **Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film** at the 74th Oscars, making it only the third Indian film ever to receive the honour. It lost to *No Man's Land*, but the nomination itself was a watershed. For diaspora families, watching Aamir Khan walk the red carpet at the Dolby Theatre was a before-and-after moment — the night Bollywood stopped being a guilty pleasure and became a point of pride.

The film swept the 47th **Filmfare Awards**, winning eight trophies including Best Film, Best Director, and Best Actor. It took home the **National Film Award for Best Popular Film**. Two decades on, it regularly appears in global lists of the greatest sports films ever made — the only cricket film to do so.

## Why This Re-Release Matters for the Diaspora

For NRIs, *Lagaan* occupies a space that few films do. It's the movie your parents rented on DVD and watched three times. It's the film you showed your American roommate to explain why cricket matters. It's the soundtrack that played at every family gathering for the better part of a decade.

A theatrical re-release, even a three-day one, is a chance to experience it the way it was meant to be seen — on a screen large enough to hold Champaner, with speakers loud enough to carry Rahman's drums across the desert. If you're in India, screenings begin June 12. If you're in the US, UK, or Canada, check your local Indian cinema listings — limited international screenings are expected, though the full overseas rollout hasn't been confirmed.

## The Reunion That's Coming

Here's the detail that turns nostalgia into anticipation: **Aamir Khan and Ashutosh Gowariker are reuniting**. Twenty-five years after *Lagaan*, the duo is developing a biopic of **Lala Amarnath**, the legendary Indian cricketer who scored India's first-ever Test century. The shoot is expected to begin around September 2026, with Rajkumar Hirani and Abhijat Joshi contributing creatively to the script.

Cricket. Aamir. Gowariker. A.R. Rahman's fingerprints likely on the music. If this feels like lightning being summoned twice to the same spot, that's because it is.

Three days. June 12 to 14. Some films get re-released because studios need the revenue. *Lagaan* gets re-released because we need it.
